**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ فَقَالَ لِصَاحِبِهِ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا﴾
The owner of the two gardens had fruit and other wealth, and he said to his believing companion while talking with him, full of vanity: "I have more wealth than you, and more mighty in supporters and helpers."

﴿وَلَوْلَا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾
If only, when you entered your garden and it pleased you, you had praised Allah and said: "This is what Allah has willed for me; I have no power to obtain it except through Allah."

﴿وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَىٰ مَا أَنفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّي أَحَدًا﴾
What the believer had said came true, and destruction struck the garden, and everything in it perished. So the disbeliever began turning his hands over in grief and regret for what he had spent on it, while it lay in ruins, part of it fallen on part, empty of what had been in it, and he said: "If only I had recognised Allah's blessings and His power, and had not associated anyone with Him." This was regret on his part when regret could no longer help him.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. When the owner of the two gardens saw his fruit, to whom did he give the credit for it? And what words did his friend show him to say when he entered his garden?
2. He said to his friend, "I have more wealth than you." Is the richer person better in the sight of Allah? (No; and being rich is not a sin, for wealth is a blessing to be thankful for. He went wrong because he forgot who had given it to him, was arrogant towards his friend, and denied the resurrection.)
3. Why did the words "If only I had not associated anyone with my Lord" not help him? And when should he have said them?

**This week's exercise**
Whenever something impresses your child this week, whether it is theirs or someone else's, they say, "Ma sha Allah, la quwwata illa billah." And at the end of each day, they tell you about one blessing and who gave it to them.
